page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-32 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the N2 machine family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor is equipped with a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI) for vector processing and machine learning acceleration, alongside AES cryptography, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 29778.72 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9659.0. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1409.48 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 23.79 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is stable, reaching 177.33 GB/sec for large block read-only operations. Notably, the server demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small LLM models, achieving 284.06 tokens per second.

Given the low memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and moderate-scale web serving. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or single-threaded legacy applications due to its memory constraints and lower single-core performance.
